    Appendix A Benchmark Details

    A.1 Data, Evaluators, and Analysis Sets

    The neutral benchmark contains 91 fixed games and five actor configurations. We match requests by the exact rule and focal-player evidence texts, deduplicate identical inputs, and require every instrument needed for a comparison. The common set has 363 unique inputs from 91 games with overall and 12-dimensional ratings from all five neutral judges and all five persona references. Overall replies with insufficient evidence remain missing; they are not replaced by zero. Persona scoring includes the completed supplementary questionnaires. Completed play includes trajectories stopped at the decision or time limit.

    The focal-player evidence records visible states, legal actions, selected actions, and outcomes. Initial play fixes seat 0 and seed 0, with random agents at other seats, limits of 500 focal decisions and four hours, and at most one model-selected recovery from an invalid action. Evaluation requests hide actor identity and collect dimensions and overall scores separately. The overall prompt concerns the recorded experience, excluding replay intention and recommendation.

    The actor configurations are GLM-5.3, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, Kimi-K2.7-Code, MiniMax-M2.5, and Qwen3.8-Max. The Qwen judge is Qwen3.8-Max-0902. The original external-rating batch requests temperature 0 for Kimi, DeepSeek, MiniMax and Qwen. Reasoning settings and output limits differ across services.

    A.2 Dimension Associations and Within-game Checks

    For each evaluator, we correlate its dimension ratings with its separately obtained overall scores, using Spearman correlation with average ranks for ties. Table 5 gives the values underlying the model rings and persona profiles in the main text. These pooled associations can reflect differences between games. To inspect variation within games, we rank scores and dimensions across the common set, subtract the corresponding game means from their ranks, and correlate the centered ranks. Table 6 reports these within-game associations. Intervals use 2,000 whole-game bootstrap samples. Simultaneous intervals account for multiple model-pair and dimension comparisons.

    Model and persona profiles.

    Across the shared inputs, mastery is positively associated with overall ratings for every model (ρ=0.413-0.574). Immersion has correlation 0.560 for GLM, compared with 0.148 for DeepSeek and 0.212 for Kimi. Challenge fit has correlations 0.419 for DeepSeek and 0.380 for MiniMax, compared with -0.003 for Kimi. For the Thrill persona, challenge fit, meaning, immersion, and emotional challenge correlate with overall ratings at 0.567, 0.571, 0.562, and 0.496, respectively; System’s emotional-challenge correlation is -0.044. These values describe pooled associations across the recorded games and trajectories.

    A.3 Scoring Level and Same-input Judgments

    We compare all ten judge pairs on each common input, yielding 3,630 comparisons. Dimension distance is the mean absolute difference across the 12 ratings. We estimate each pair’s usual signed overall-score difference from all other games, weighting games equally, subtract this offset from the held-out comparison, and then take the absolute adjusted gap. Bootstrap samples refit the offset while excluding every copy of the held-out game. Applying thresholds of dimension MAE at most 0.5 and overall gap at least three identifies 63 pairs from 43 inputs and 30 games. For the 1,834 pairs with dimension MAE at most 0.5, the share with gap at least two falls from 31.5% to 8.8% after adjustment. The reduction is 22.6 percentage points. For a gap of at least three, the corresponding shares are 3.4% and 1.4%.

    In Authors, 26 successful requests produce a 13-0 win. GLM assigns 7 for smooth progress, whereas Qwen assigns 2 and emphasizes limited challenge and uncertainty. In Palace, Kimi assigns 3 and emphasizes the loss and slow hand reduction; MiniMax assigns 7 and values varied, coherent interaction. In Cold Hands Poker, one forced ante ends at a focal payoff of -5: DeepSeek assigns 5 for an empty but not actively frustrating experience, whereas Qwen assigns 2 for a lack of meaningful play. In Arlington, GLM assigns 8 and values agency and progress, whereas DeepSeek assigns 5 because procedural evidence offers limited support for strong subjective engagement.

    For each game and judge, we subtract its average rating of other actors from its rating of its own actor’s trajectory. We then subtract the panel’s mean contrast for that actor.     Evaluation resemblance and output endorsement are matched on all 91 benchmark games, covering 363 unique inputs. For a model-persona pair, evaluation resemblance is the Spearman correlation of their overall ratings, centered over personas within the model. Output endorsement is the persona’s rating of that model’s play after removing game-specific model and persona mean effects.
